syllabusTopics: Random variable and its probability distribution
Mean, variance and standard deviation of a random variable
agentNotes: Authoring contract: frontend/AGENTS.md §9. Filled 2026-10-06 (Class 12 track); no Class-12 PYQ bank in-corpus, so the board row is NEB-style with no fabricated citation.

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Conditional probability P(A|B) re-weights the world given B; independence factorises (P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B)); Bayes flips conditions — from P(test|disease) to P(disease|test) — via prior-weighted partitions. Random variables tabulate outcomes with probabilities (mean = ΣxP, variance = Σx²P − mean²); Bernoulli trials compound into binomial B(n,p) (mean np, variance npq) and rare events into Poisson (mean = variance = λ).

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B)  ·  Bayes: P(Eᵢ|A) = P(Eᵢ)P(A|Eᵢ) / ΣP(Eⱼ)P(A|Eⱼ)  ·  E(X) = Σx·P(x) · Var = Σx²P − μ²  ·  binomial: P(r) = C(n,r)pʳqⁿ⁻ʳ, μ = np, σ² = npq  ·  Poisson: P(r) = e^(−λ)λʳ/r!, μ = σ² = λ

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Bayes needs a PARTITION (exhaustive, exclusive hypotheses) plus likelihoods. Binomial needs fixed n, two outcomes, constant p, independence. Poisson needs rare events in continuum (n large, p small, λ = np moderate). Independence must be verified, never assumed from wording alone.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Disease-testing paradox: 99%-accurate test on 0.1%-prevalence disease still yields mostly false positives — priors dominate (the Bayes lesson). Poisson models misprints-per-page, calls-per-hour. Mean = variance flags Poisson data; binomial variance always trails its mean (×q).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Two-machine Bayes template: machines A/B make 60%/40% of items with 2%/5% defect rates; a defective item appears → P(A|defective) = (0.6×0.02)/(0.6×0.02 + 0.4×0.05) = 0.012/0.032 = 0.375. Numerator = one branch, denominator = all branches — total probability below, target branch above.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Bayes outputs posteriors only as good as priors (garbage priors, garbage posteriors — sensitivity analysis answers). Binomial/Poisson idealise (constant p, homogeneity); real trials drift. Mean/variance summaries hide distribution shape (same μ,σ², different stories).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Bayes from the multiplication theorem written both ways: P(Eᵢ∩A) = P(Eᵢ)P(A|Eᵢ) = P(A)P(Eᵢ|A) → divide by P(A), expand P(A) over the partition (total probability) → the theorem. Binomial from counting: C(n,r) sequences each with probability pʳqⁿ⁻ʳ; mean/variance via indicator sums (linearity + independence).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'Given that' → conditional/Bayes tree immediately. Partition first (machines/urns/diseases), likelihoods second, Bayes fraction third. Distribution ID: counts in fixed trials → binomial; rare over time/space → Poisson; verify mean–variance signature.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: Bayes two-branch numericals (factory/disease templates); binomial mean/variance + term probabilities; Poisson rare-event applications; random-variable E(X)/Var(X) tables.
